quick_skim.title: Randomization Inference for Matched Pairs with Binary Outcomes
quick_skim.abstract: We give an exact randomization-based confidence set for the average treatment effect (ATE) in matched-pair studies with a binary outcome, requiring neither monotonicity nor any distributional assumption beyond the within-pair coin flip. At its core is an analytic solution to the worst-case allocation of attributable effects: two binomial-symmetry lemmas identify the pattern hardest to reject as a single boundary corner, so testing null hypotheses needs no integer program and no numerical search. Inverting the test via binary search yields a prediction set for the attributable effect in O(log S) Binomial tail calculations; the Bonferroni proposition of Rigdon and Hudgens (2015) produces the ATE confidence set at the same computational cost. The same corner extends without further machinery to a sensitivity analysis for matched observational studies under Rosenbaum's $Γ$-model. A simple formula for the design sensitivity illuminates when an observational study can hope to provide evidence for an effect.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Develops exact randomization-based confidence sets for average treatment effects in matched-pair binary-outcome studies, using binomial-symmetry lemmas and binary search without monotonicity assumptions.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 在匹配对设计中评价平均处理效应常依赖单调性且计算复杂。该文利用两条二项对称性引理将最难拒绝模式刻画为单个角落，无需整数规划或数值搜索即可完成随机化检验，再通过二分检索得到置信集，计算成本仅为对数次二项尾概率。该方法不要求单调性或额外分布假设，可稳健地用于社会支持对老年抑郁等二值结局的保护效应评估；但论文本身未涉及具体人群数据。
